slice.result: The canonical cargo-vendor document exists at the pinned commit. It states that cargo vendor vendors crates.io and git dependencies into a local directory and prints configuration for using those vendored sources. Its --offline mode prevents network access and restricts resolution to crates already downloaded locally; the same document points to cargo fetch for downloading dependencies before going offline. --frozen combines --locked and --offline.
slice.inference: This supports a narrow use-time/local-reuse mechanism: with a complete local Cargo cache, offline/frozen vendoring can avoid network access while materializing local vendored sources. It does not establish how a complete dependency cache is initially created without prior network or execution, so bootstrap parity remains unresolved.
